nodes.name: Eben tree
nodes.desc: A common rainforest tree of the Gabon region whose oily fruit is eaten by chimpanzees and other animals; GBIF records its relatives (Pachylobus) as the most-recorded plants near the park.

nodes.name: Strombosia trees
nodes.desc: Understory and mid-canopy rainforest trees whose fruit is eaten by chimpanzees and guenons, according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Fig trees fruit through much of the year in African rainforest, feeding monkeys, apes, elephants and birds.

nodes.name: Marantaceae herbs
nodes.desc: Broad-leaved herbs of the forest floor and clearings; stems and leaves feed gorillas and elephants in Central African forests.

nodes.name: African forest elephant
nodes.desc: Eats bark, leaves and many fruits and carries large seeds for kilometres in its dung, shaping which trees regrow. It also keeps trails open through dense forest.

nodes.name: Western lowland gorilla
nodes.desc: Mainly eats fruit, shoots, leaves and herbaceous stems, switching toward leaves and herbs when fruit is scarce. Listed among the primates of Monte Alen.

nodes.name: Moustached guenon
nodes.desc: A small forest monkey that eats fruit and insects; GloBI records it feeding on Strombosia fruit near the park.

nodes.name: Black colobus
nodes.desc: A leaf- and seed-eating monkey of Central African forest, named among the primates of Monte Alen National Park.

nodes.name: Mandrill
nodes.desc: A large ground-living monkey of the forest that eats fruit, seeds and invertebrates. Recorded near the park and listed among its primates.

nodes.name: Bay duiker
nodes.desc: A small forest antelope that feeds on fallen fruit and leaves on the forest floor. It is prey for leopards and crowned eagles.

nodes.name: Yellow-whiskered greenbul
nodes.desc: The most-recorded bird near the park. It eats fruit and insects and so helps spread seeds.

nodes.name: Forest insects and termites
nodes.desc: Beetles, ants, termites and other insects feed on plants and leaf litter and are food for primates, frogs and birds.

nodes.name: Central chimpanzee
nodes.desc: Mostly a fruit eater, with fruit about 60% of the diet, but it also eats insects and occasionally hunts red colobus monkeys. Recorded near the park.

nodes.name: Goliath frog
nodes.desc: The largest frog in the world; it lives in fast rivers in the southern part of the park and is protected from hunting. It eats insects and other small animals.

nodes.name: Jameson's mamba
nodes.desc: A tree-living venomous snake recorded near the park that hunts birds, small mammals and lizards.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: Takes mostly medium-sized forest prey such as duikers and guenons and caches larger kills away from rivals.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: A forest eagle that hunts monkeys, mostly guenons, and small antelopes such as duikers from perches below the canopy.

nodes.name: Equatorial sunlight
nodes.desc: Year-round light, but the closed canopy leaves little for the forest floor.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Roughly 3,000 to 3,500 mm of rain falls each year in the park, feeding rivers and Lake Atoc.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and fallen wood are recycled quickly into the soil in the humid forest.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites and litter microbes
nodes.desc: Fungi, termites and microbes break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
